The split is right: keep a private local copy automatically, with Internet Archive submission as an explicit option. For a normal page, the local copy should be a self-contained single HTML file so it still works independently; for a PDF, preserve the actual PDF file.

Capture it once when I save the bookmark and don’t silently replace it later—the point is to preserve what I originally saw. A failed capture can be retried once the page becomes available. Archiving a bookmark must keep its saved copy, while permanently deleting the bookmark should remove that copy too.

With those details, preservation feels right.
